                                    </table>
                                    <p>Type 2
                                    </p>
                                    <table border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="margin: 1em 1em 1em 0; background: #f9f9f9; border: 1px #aaa solid; border-collapse: collapse;">
                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>b1</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>b0</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Function</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Read/Write</i>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>Select internal 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Write Only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>Write to selected internal 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Write Only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>-</td>
                                                <td>-
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>

                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>Read from selected internal 6845 register</td>

                                                </td>

                                    <p>Type 3 and 4
                                    </p>
                                    <table border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="margin: 1em 1em 1em 0; background: #f9f9f9; border: 1px #aaa solid; border-collapse: collapse;">
                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>b1</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>b0</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Function</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Read/Write</i>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>Select internal 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Write Only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>Write to selected internal 6845 register</td>

                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                        </tbody>
                                    </table>
                                    <p>It is not possible to read from all the internal registers, this table shows the read/write status of each register for each type: 
                                    </p>
                                    <table border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="margin: 1em 1em 1em 0; background: #f9f9f9; border: 1px #aaa solid; border-collapse: collapse;">

                                            <tr>

                                    <p>
                                        <b>Notes</b>
                                    </p>
                                    <p>1. On type 0 and 1, if a Write Only register is read from, "0" is returned.

                                    <p>2. See the document "Extra CPC Plus Hardware Information" for more details.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>3. CRTC type 4 is the same as CRTC type 3. The registers also repeat as they do on the type 3.
                                    </p>

                            <section id="citizen-section-20" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="Horizontal_and_Vertical_Sync_.28R3.29"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Horizontal_and_Vertical_Sync_(R3)">Horizontal and Vertical Sync (R3)</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <section id="citizen-section-21" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span id="Horizontal_and_Vertical_Sync_.28R3.29_2"></span>
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Horizontal_and_Vertical_Sync_(R3)_2">Horizontal and Vertical Sync (R3)</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>Type 0:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..4 define Vertical Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, this gives 16 lines of VSYNC.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 3..0 define Horizontal Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, no HSYNC is generated (and therefore, no interrupts).</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>Type 1:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..4 are ignored. Vertical Sync is fixed at 16 lines.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 3..0 define Horizontal Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, no HSYNC is generated (and therefore, no interrupts).</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>Type 2:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..4 are ignored. Vertical Sync is fixed at 16 lines.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 3..0 define Horizontal Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, this gives a HSYNC width of 16.</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>Types 3/4:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..4 define Vertical Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, this gives 16 lines of VSYNC.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 3..0 define Horizontal Sync Width. If 0 is programmed, this gives a HSYNC width of 16.</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-22" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span id="Interlace_and_Skew_.28R8.29"></span>
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Interlace_and_Skew_(R8)">Interlace and Skew (R8)</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>Types 0/3/4:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..6 define the skew (delay) of the CUDISP signal (00 = Non-skew ; 01 = One-character skew ; 10 = Two-character skew ; 11 = Non-output).</li>
                                                <li>Bits 5..4 define the skew (delay) of the DISPTMG signal (00 = Non-skew ; 01 = One-character skew ; 10 = Two-character skew ; 11 = Non-output).</li>
                                                <li>Bits 3..2 are ignored.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 1..0 define the interlace mode (00 = No Interlace ; 01 = Interlace Sync ; 10 = No Interlace ; 11 = Interlace Sync and Video).</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>Types 1/2:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>Bits 7..2 are ignored.</li>
                                                <li>Bits 1..0 define the interlace mode.</li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-23" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="R31_on_Type_1">R31 on Type 1</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>R31 is described in the UM6845R documentation as "Dummy Register".
                                            </p>
                                            <p>Its use is described in the documentation for the Rockwell R6545 in combination with R18, R19 and R8 and the Status Register.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>In the UM6845R it appears to have no effect. Reading and writing does nothing. Reading it returns &amp;FF.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>R31 doesn't exist on CRTCs 0/2/3/4.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-24" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="UM6845R_and_R12.2FR13"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="UM6845R_and_R12/R13">UM6845R and R12/R13</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>The UM6845R differs to other CRTC in respect of R12/R13. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>When VCC=0, R12/R13 is re-read at the start of each line. R12/R13 can therefore be changed for each scanline when VCC=0. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>Just like other CRTCs when RC==(R9-1), the current MA is captured for the next char-line.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>In demos to make a display compatible with all CRTCs program R12/R13 when VCC!=0. This will then take effect at the next frame start.
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-25" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="UM6845R_status_register">UM6845R status register</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>The UM6845R has a status register that can be read using port &amp;BExx.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>Bit 6 is set to 1 if there is a strobe input to the /LPEN signal. It is cleared to 0 when either R17 or R16 (LPEN address) of the CRTC are read. It signals there is a valid LPEN input. On my CPC (arnoldemu) with UM6845R, it is triggered at power on, R17 and R16 have the values 0 when read.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>Bit 5 is set to 1 when CRTC is in "vertical blanking". Vertical blanking is when the vertical border is active. i.e. VCC>=R6. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>It is cleared when the frame is started (VCC=0). It is not directly related to the DISPTMG output (used by the CPC to display the border colour) because that output is a combination of horizontal and vertical blanking.
                                    This bit will be 0 when pixels are being displayed.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>All the other bits read as 0 and don't have any function.
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-26" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="CRTC_Type_Detection">CRTC Type Detection</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>It is possible to detect the CRTC Type using software methods, and this is done to: 
                                    </p>
                                    <ul>
                                        <li>warn that the software was not designed for the detected 6845 and may function incorrectly</li>
                                        <li>to adapt the software so that it will run with the detected 6845</li>
                                        <li>In most cases, the type of the detected 6845 is reported</li>
                                    </ul>
                                    <p>Detection routine in BASIC:
                                    </p>
                                    <pre>10 MODE 1:' Reinitialize screen
                                    20 OUT &amp;BC00,31:IF INP(&amp;BF00)=255 THEN PRINT"crtc 1":END
                                    30 OUT &amp;BC00,12:IF INP(&amp;BF00)=0 THEN PRINT"crtc 2":END
                                    40 OUT &amp;BC00,20:IF INP(&amp;BF00)=0 THEN PRINT"crtc 0":END
                                    50 PRINT"crtc 3/4"
                                    </pre>
                                    <p>
                                        Distinguishing between CRTCs 3 and 4 can be done by trying to 
                                        <a href="/index.php/Programming:Unlocking_ASIC" title="Programming:Unlocking ASIC">unlock the ASIC</a>
                                         or by testing the 
                                        <a href="/index.php/8255" title="8255">PPI chip</a>
                                        . On ASIC, if PPI Port B is set as output it will behave the same as input.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>

                            <section id="citizen-section-29" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="CRTC-II_.28aka_Type_5.29"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="CRTC-II_(aka_Type_5)">CRTC-II (aka Type 5)</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>
                                        The 
                                        <a href="/imgs/b/bc/CRTC-5-HD6345.pdf" class="internal" title="CRTC-5-HD6345.pdf">HD6345 datasheet</a>
                                         states it is upward-compatible with the HD6845S in pin and software.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>This chip was never used by Amstrad. However, some CPC enthusiasts have replaced the original CRTC chip in their CPC with this one.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        With this chip, split-screen becomes easy: 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://thecheshirec.at/2024/05/20/des-splitscreens-en-basic-sur-crtc5/">Split-screen in BASIC</a>
                                        . And 3 new graphics modes (160x100x16c, 320x100x4c, 640x100x2c) are available: 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://thecheshirec.at/2024/11/10/trois-nouveaux-modes-video-grace-au-crtc-5/">New graphics modes in BASIC</a>
                                        .
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        This is the cheapest way to upgrade the CPC's graphics capabilities, costing only 1.29€. 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://thecheshirec.at/2024/05/19/des-crtc5-a-129e/">Source</a>
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>

    <script>
    window.clientPrefs = () => {
        let className = document.documentElement.className;
        let storage;
        try {
            storage = localStorage.getItem('mwclientpreferences');
        } catch (e) {}
        if (storage) {
            storage.split(',').forEach((pref) => {
                const pattern = new RegExp('(^| )' + pref.replace(/-clientpref-\w+$|[^\w-]+/g, '') + '-clientpref-\\w+( |$)');
                if (pattern.test(className)) {
                    className = className.replace(pattern, '$1' + pref + '$2');
                } else {
                    className += ' ' + pref;
                }
            });
            document.documentElement.className = className;
        }
    };
    (() => {
        window.clientPrefs();
    })();
    </script>

                                    <a href="/index.php/File:CRTC_Type_0.jpg" class="mw-file-description">
                                        <img src="/imgs/thumb/0/0d/CRTC_Type_0.jpg/300px-CRTC_Type_0.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="105" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/imgs/thumb/0/0d/CRTC_Type_0.jpg/450px-CRTC_Type_0.jpg 1.5x, /imgs/thumb/0/0d/CRTC_Type_0.jpg/600px-CRTC_Type_0.jpg 2x"/>
                                    </a>
                                    <figcaption>CRTC Type 0 (Hitachi)</figcaption>
                                </figure>
                                <figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb">
                                    <a href="/index.php/File:CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png" class="mw-file-description">
                                        <img src="/imgs/thumb/d/d5/CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png/300px-CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="143" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/imgs/thumb/d/d5/CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png/450px-CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png 1.5x, /imgs/d/d5/CRTC_UMC_Type_0.png 2x"/>
                                    </a>
                                    <figcaption>CRTC Type 0 (UMC)</figcaption>
                                </figure>
                                <figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb">
                                    <a href="/index.php/File:CRTC_Type_1.png" class="mw-file-description">
                                        <img src="/imgs/thumb/f/ff/CRTC_Type_1.png/300px-CRTC_Type_1.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="136" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/imgs/thumb/f/ff/CRTC_Type_1.png/450px-CRTC_Type_1.png 1.5x, /imgs/thumb/f/ff/CRTC_Type_1.png/600px-CRTC_Type_1.png 2x"/>
                                    </a>
                                    <figcaption>CRTC Type 1</figcaption>
                                </figure>
                                <figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb">
                                    <a href="/index.php/File:CRTC6845-Type2.jpg" class="mw-file-description">
                                        <img src="/imgs/thumb/b/b2/CRTC6845-Type2.jpg/300px-CRTC6845-Type2.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="158" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/imgs/thumb/b/b2/CRTC6845-Type2.jpg/450px-CRTC6845-Type2.jpg 1.5x, /imgs/thumb/b/b2/CRTC6845-Type2.jpg/600px-CRTC6845-Type2.jpg 2x"/>
                                    </a>
                                    <figcaption>CRTC Type 2</figcaption>
                                </figure>
                                <p>
                                    The 6845 
                                    <b>CRTC</b>
                                     (Cathode Ray Tube Controller) chip was created by Motorola in 1977. It works with the 
                                    <a href="/index.php/Gate_Array" title="Gate Array">Gate Array</a>
                                     to generate the video signal on the Amstrad CPC.
                                </p>
                                <p>
                                    This chip is also used in the 
                                    <a href="/index.php/BBC_Micro" title="BBC Micro">BBC Micro</a>
                                    , 
                                    <a href="/index.php/Lynx" title="Lynx">Camputers Lynx</a>
                                    , 
                                    <a href="/index.php/EG2000_Colour_Genie" title="EG2000 Colour Genie">EG2000 Colour Genie</a>
                                    , 
                                    <a href="/index.php?title=Sharp_X1&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Sharp X1 (page does not exist)">Sharp X1</a>
                                    , 
                                    <a href="/index.php?title=MicroBee&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="MicroBee (page does not exist)">MicroBee</a>
                                    , 
                                    <a href="/index.php?title=Commodore_PET&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Commodore PET (page does not exist)">Commodore PET</a>
                                     and the early graphics cards (MDA, Hercules, CGA, Plantronics Colorplus) for 
                                    <a href="/index.php?title=IBM_PC&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="IBM PC (page does not exist)">IBM PC</a>
                                    . And it is found in some 
                                    <a class="external text" href="https://www.msx.org/wiki/Hitachi_HD6845">MSX1 expansions</a>
                                    , providing an 80-column text mode.
                                </p>
                                <p>It's important to note that the CRTC chip is primarily designed for character-based displays. It explains why, on the Amstrad CPC, the video memory is organized into a grid of characters rather than a purely linear bitmap.
                                </p>
                                <p>NOTE: This document describes the functionality in terms of the CPC with its separate CRTC and Gate-Array. The Plus has both integrated into the same IC, but could be considered to have two functional blocks, one for CRTC and one for Gate-Array. In this document the term 'Gate-Array' is used, but this also applies to the ASIC.
                                </p>
                                <meta property="mw:PageProp/toc"/>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-1" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Overview">Overview</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>The 6845 Cathode Ray Tube Controller (CRTC) is a programmable IC used to generate video displays. This IC is used in a variety of computers including the Amstrad CPC, Amstrad CPC+ and KC Compact. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The CRTC is a simple chip. It is made up of counters and equality operators, tied by simple logic. All the complexity stems from its multiple independent implementations with their subtle differences.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The CRTC was a common part available from many different manufacturers. During the life of the CPC, Amstrad sourced the CRTC from various manufacturers. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>All ICs used were based on the same design but have a different implementation. As a result they do not operate identically in all situations. This document highlights these differences. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>This table lists the known ICs used, with their part number, manufacturer and type number. 
                                    </p>
                                    <table border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="margin: 1em 1em 1em 0; background: #f9f9f9; border: 1px #aaa solid; border-collapse: collapse;">
                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Part number</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Manufacturer</i>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <i>Type number (note 3)</i>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>HD6845S</td>
                                                <td>Hitachi</td>
                                                <td>0
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>UM6845</td>
                                                <td>UMC</td>
                                                <td>0
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>UM6845R</td>
                                                <td>UMC</td>
                                                <td>1
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>MC6845</td>
                                                <td>Motorola</td>
                                                <td>2
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>AMS40489</td>
                                                <td>Amstrad</td>
                                                <td>3 (note 1)
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>40226</td>
                                                <td>Amstrad</td>
                                                <td>4 (note 2)
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                        </tbody>
                                    </table>
                                    <p>
                                        <b>NOTES</b>
                                    </p>
                                    <p>1. The CRTC functionality is integrated into the CPC+ ASIC. This type exists only in the CPC464+,CPC6128+ and GX4000. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>2. This type exists in "cost-down" CPC464 and CPC6128 systems. In the "cost-down" the CRTC functionality is integrated into a single ASIC IC. This ASIC is often refered to as the "Pre-ASIC" because it preceeded the CPC+ ASIC. The CRTC functionality of the Pre-ASIC is almost identical to the CRTC within the ASIC.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>3. In the Amstrad community each 6845 implementation has been assigned a type number. This type identifies a group of implementations which operate in exactly the same way. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>As far as I know, the type number system was originally used by demo programmers. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>It is possible to detect the 6845 present using software methods, and this is done to: 
                                    </p>
                                    <ul>
                                        <li>warn that the software was not designed for the detected 6845 and may function incorrectly,</li>
                                        <li>to adapt the software so that it will run with the detected 6845</li>
                                        <li>In most cases, the type of the detected 6845 is reported.</li>
                                    </ul>
                                    <p>4. As far as I know, the KC compact used HD6845R only.
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-2" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Timings_and_relating_with_Z80_instructions_count">Timings and relating with Z80 instructions count</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>
                                        Some informations like : how many Z80 instructions can I fit within a scan line ? Within a screen ? Etc... See 
                                        <a class="external free" href="https://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/frame-flyback-and-interrupts/msg25106/#msg25106">http://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/frame-flyback-and-interrupts/msg25106/#msg25106</a>

                                        (To be extracted/edited to conform to wiki good practices).
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-3" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Programming">Programming</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>The 6845 is selected when bit 14 of the I/O port address is set to "0". Bit 9 and 8 of the I/O port address define the function to access. The remaining bits can be any value, but it is adviseable to set these to "1" to avoid conflict with other devices in the system.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The recommended I/O port addresses are:
                                    </p>
                                    <table class="wikitable">

                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <th>I/O port address
                                                </th>
                                                <th>/CS (A14)
                                                </th>
                                                <th>R/W (A9)
                                                </th>
                                                <th>RS (A8)
                                                </th>
                                                <th>Function
                                                </th>
                                                <th>Read/Write
                                                </th>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>&amp;BCxx</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>Select 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Write only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>&amp;BDxx</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>Write to selected internal 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Write only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>&amp;BExx</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <ul>
                                                        <li>CRTCs 0/2: —</li>
                                                        <li>CRTC 1: Read Status Register</li>
                                                        <li>CRTCs 3/4: Read from selected internal 6845 register</li>
                                                    </ul>
                                                </td>
                                                <td>Read only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>&amp;BFxx</td>
                                                <td>0</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>1</td>
                                                <td>Read from selected internal 6845 register</td>
                                                <td>Read only
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                        </tbody>
                                    </table>
                                    <p>The CRTC is not connected to the CPU's RD and WR pins, so it cannot detect the bus's I/O direction. Therefore, executing an IN instruction to the select or write functions causes the CRTC to write the unpredictable data provided by the high-impedance bus to its registers.
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-4" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Addressing">Addressing</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>
                                        The VMA of the 
                                        <a href="/index.php/Gate_Array" title="Gate Array">Gate Array</a>
                                         is constructed from the CRTC MA and RA signals:
                                    </p>
                                    <table class="wikitable">

                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <th>Video Memory Address
                                                </th>
                                                <th>Signal source
                                                </th>
                                                <th>Signal name
                                                </th>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A15</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA13
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A14</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA12
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A13</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <b>RA2</b>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A12</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <b>RA1</b>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A11</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>
                                                    <b>RA0</b>
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A10</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA9
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A9</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA8
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A8</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA7
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A7</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA6
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A6</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA5
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A5</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA4
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A4</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA3
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A3</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA2
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A2</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA1
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A1</td>
                                                <td>6845</td>
                                                <td>MA0
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>A0</td>
                                                <td>Gate-Array</td>
                                                <td>CCLK
                                                </td>
                                            </tr>
                                        </tbody>
                                    </table>
                                    <p>CRTC generates the address, Gate Array reads the data and converts it to pixels based on its current graphics mode and palette.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>CRTC pins RA3, RA4, MA10, MA11 are not connected on CPC.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-5" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Overscan_bits">Overscan bits</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>
                                                It is possible to use 32KB screen size (used for 
                                                <a href="/index.php/Programming:Overscan" title="Programming:Overscan">overscan</a>
                                                ) by setting bits 11 and 10 of Register 12 both to 1. Bits MA11 and MA10 of the address generated by the CRTC are not written on the address bus to access video memory; settings both bits to 1 is the only way to cause a carry to bit MA12 when address pass over the end of current video page to change the memory address to the next video page.
                                            </p>
                                            <table class="wikitable">
                                                <caption>CRTC Display Start Address
                                                </caption>
                                                <tbody>
                                                    <tr>
                                                        <th colspan="8">Register 12
                                                        </th>
                                                        <th colspan="8">Register 13
                                                        </th>
                                                    </tr>
                                                    <tr>
                                                        <th>15</th>
                                                        <th>14</th>
                                                        <th>13</th>
                                                        <th>12</th>
                                                        <th>11</th>
                                                        <th>10</th>
                                                        <th>9</th>
                                                        <th>8
                                                        </th>
                                                        <th>7</th>
                                                        <th>6</th>
                                                        <th>5</th>
                                                        <th>4</th>
                                                        <th>3</th>
                                                        <th>2</th>
                                                        <th>1</th>
                                                        <th>0
                                                        </th>
                                                    </tr>
                                                    <tr>
                                                        <td colspan="2">Unused
                                                        </td>
                                                        <td colspan="2">Video Page
                                                        </td>
                                                        <td colspan="2">Page Size
                                                        </td>
                                                        <td colspan="10">Start Address (1024 positions)
                                                        </td>
                                                    </tr>
                                                </tbody>
                                            </table>
                                            <table style="white-space: nowrap;">

                                                <tbody>
                                                    <tr>
                                                        <td>
                                                            <table class="wikitable" style="margin-right: 32px">

                                                                <tbody>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <th>Bit 13</th>
                                                                        <th>Bit 12</th>
                                                                        <th>Video Page
                                                                        </th>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>0000 - 3FFF
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>4000 - 7FFF
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>8000 - BFFF
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>C000 - FFFF
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                </tbody>
                                                            </table>
                                                        </td>
                                                        <td>
                                                            <table class="wikitable">

                                                                <tbody>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <th>Bit 11</th>
                                                                        <th>Bit 10</th>
                                                                        <th>Page Size
                                                                        </th>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>16KB
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>16KB
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>0</td>
                                                                        <td>16KB
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                    <tr>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>1</td>
                                                                        <td>
                                                                            <b>32KB</b>
                                                                        </td>
                                                                    </tr>
                                                                </tbody>
                                                            </table>
                                                        </td>
                                                    </tr>
                                                </tbody>
                                            </table>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-6" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Coarse_hardware_scrolling">Coarse hardware scrolling</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>The start address can be manipulated to achieve horizontal and/or vertical hardware scrolling:
                                            </p>
                                            <ul>
                                                <li>
                                                    To move right: 
                                                    <code>start_address := start_address + 1</code>
                                                </li>
                                                <li>
                                                    To move left: 
                                                    <code>start_address := start_address - 1</code>
                                                </li>
                                                <li>
                                                    To move down: 
                                                    <code>start_address := start_address + R1</code>
                                                </li>
                                                <li>
                                                    To move up: 
                                                    <code>start_address := start_address - R1</code>
                                                </li>
                                            </ul>
                                            <p>However, it is a position in word (16 bits), not in byte. So, the screen will move two bytes at a time horizontally. Also, the precision will be one CRTC character vertically.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                The first game that used R12/R13 for both horizontal and vertical hardware scrolling is 
                                                <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpc-power.com/index.php?page=detail&amp;num=1839">Roland on the Ropes</a>
                                                , released in 1984.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>The following BASIC program demonstrates the coarse scrolling by setting the R12 and R13 registers based on keyboard input:
                                            </p>
                                            <pre>10 ma%=0
                                            20 IF INKEY(1)=0 THEN GOSUB 100
                                            30 IF INKEY(2)=0 THEN GOSUB 300
                                            40 IF INKEY(8)=0 THEN GOSUB 500
                                            50 IF INKEY(0)=0 THEN GOSUB 700
                                            60 GOTO 20
                                            100 ' right
                                            110 ma%=ma%+1: GOSUB 900: RETURN
                                            300 ' down
                                            310 ma%=ma%+40: GOSUB 900: RETURN
                                            500 ' left
                                            510 ma%=ABS(ma%-1): GOSUB 900: RETURN
                                            700 ' up
                                            710 ma%=ABS(ma%-40): GOSUB 900: RETURN
                                            900 ' set R12 and R13
                                            910 l%=ma% AND 255: h%=&amp;30 OR ((ma%\256) AND 3) :OUT &amp;BC00,13:OUT &amp;BD00,l%: OUT &amp;BC00,12:OUT &amp;BD00,h%
                                            930 RETURN
                                            </pre>
                                            <p>Which looks like the following:
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File">
                                                    <a href="/index.php/File:CRTC-Coarse-scroll.gif" class="mw-file-description">
                                                        <img src="/imgs/4/4b/CRTC-Coarse-scroll.gif" decoding="async" width="768" height="540" class="mw-file-element"/>
                                                    </a>
                                                </span>
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-7" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Advanced_hardware_scrolling">Advanced hardware scrolling</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>To achieve smoother hardware scrolling, other tricks are required in complement to R12/R13. Usually, R3 is used for smooth horizontal scroll and R5 for smooth vertical scroll.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                A good example of smooth hardware multidirectional scrolling game on CPC is 
                                                <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpc-power.com/index.php?page=detail&amp;num=2119">Super Cauldron</a>
                                                , released in 1993.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                Everything you need to know about hardware scrolling on CPC can be found 
                                                <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/hardware-scrolling-21687/">there</a>
                                                .
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-8" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="Split_screen_.28aka_Rupture.29"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Split_screen_(aka_Rupture)">Split screen (aka Rupture)</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>While there is usually 1 CRTC frame per screen frame, the screen frame can be divided into multiple CRTC frames of varying proportions.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        This is useful for defining different scrolling zones in your screen frame. For example, it was used for hardware parallax scrolling in the game 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpc-power.com/index.php?page=detail&amp;num=1307">The Living Daylights</a>
                                        , released in 1987. 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/the-living-daylights-extra-colours-in-mode-1-rasters-screen-splits/">Source</a>
                                    </p>
                                    <p>And this is basically the bread and butter of innumerable CPC demos.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        Some rules of thumb 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/advice-on-split-screen-code/msg242186/">Source</a>
                                        :
                                    </p>
                                    <ul>
                                        <li>changes to the screen address have to be done anywhere in the previous split</li>
                                        <li>changes to the height of the split have to be done inside the current split (after it has started, in the area of the size of the previous split)</li>
                                        <li>changes to screen mode and colours are happening immediately</li>
                                    </ul>
                                    <p>CRTC registers and screen splitting:
                                    </p>
                                    <ul>
                                        <li>reg 0 (63) = x-screenwidth (usually always 63)</li>
                                        <li>reg 1 (50) = x-splitwidth (e.g.50)</li>
                                        <li>reg 2 (51) = x-splitstart (e.g. 51)</li>
                                        <li>reg 3 (08) = x-finestart (maybe use this for half-char scrolling)</li>
                                        <li>reg 4 (##) = y-splitheight-1 (set this inside the current split)</li>
                                        <li>reg 5 (00) = y-finestart</li>
                                        <li>reg 6 (25) = y-max visible splitpart (same like 4)</li>
                                        <li>reg 7 (##) = inside last split -> set to 0; inside first split, but after vblank -> set to 255</li>
                                        <li>reg 9 (07) = y-lines/char-1</li>
                                    </ul>
                                    <p>Set this inside the previous split:
                                    </p>
                                    <ul>
                                        <li>reg12 (##) = address high (char / 256 + block * 16)</li>
                                        <li>reg13 (##) = address low  (char mod 256)</li>
                                    </ul>
                                    <p>Total height of all splits must be 39.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        The 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpcwiki.eu/forum/programming/interrupt-positions-with-various-sized-screens/">IntPos tool</a>
                                         by Kevin Thacker can help visualize the potential split screen areas.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        Note: If all you want is multiple graphics modes in the same frame, you don't need to touch the CRTC at all. More information here: 
                                        <a class="external text" href="https://www.cpc-power.com/cpcarchives/index.php?page=articles&amp;num=184">Multi-Mode Graphique (FR)</a>
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-9" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="CUDISP_.28aka_CURSOR.29"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="CUDISP_(aka_CURSOR)">CUDISP (aka CURSOR)</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>CUDISP (Cursor Display) signal defines the hardware cursor.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>CRTC pin CUDISP is not connected to the Gate Array, so it has no effect on a barebone CPC or Plus machine.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        However, this signal is provided to the 
                                        <a href="/index.php/Connector:Expansion_port" title="Connector:Expansion port">Connector:Expansion port</a>
                                        . And it is used by the 
                                        <a href="/index.php/PlayCity" title="PlayCity">PlayCity</a>
                                         and 
                                        <a href="/index.php/Play2CPC" title="Play2CPC">Play2CPC</a>
                                         expansions.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-10" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span id="DISPTMG_.28aka_Display_Enable.29"></span>
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="DISPTMG_(aka_Display_Enable)">DISPTMG (aka Display Enable)</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>DISPTMG (Display Timing) signal defines the border. When DISPTMG is "0" the border colour is output by the Gate Array to the display.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The border has higher priority than pixels but lower priority than the black colour output when HSYNC/VSYNC are active.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>While border is active, all the CRTC counters continue to increment normally and addresses continue to be generated.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The DISPTMG signal is composited from its 3 internal subcomponents: HBORDER (Horizontal), VBORDER (Vertical), SBORDER (Split) by using the NOR function. DISPTMG is "0" if at least one of its subcomponents is "1". These 3 subcomponents are all independent of each other.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>
                                        <br/>
                                    </p>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-11" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="HBORDER">HBORDER</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>On all CRTCs, HBORDER is disabled when HCC=0 and enabled when HCC=R1.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>The exception is for CRTC2 during an HSYNC: the HCC=0 check is skipped, so HBORDER stays on.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-12" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="VBORDER">VBORDER</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>On all CRTCs, VBORDER is disabled when VCC=0 and enabled when VCC=R6.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>On CRTCs 0/1/2, the condition VCC=R6 is tested on every cycle.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>On CRTCs 3/4, the condition VCC=R6 is tested only at each new character line start (when VLC=0 and HCC=0).
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-13" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="SBORDER">SBORDER</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>
                                                Split border is a technique similar to split rasters, except that it is handled by the CRTC instead of the 
                                                <a href="/index.php/Gate_Array" title="Gate Array">Gate Array</a>
                                                .
                                            </p>
                                            <p>DISPTMG can be temporarily forced to 0 by using R8 (DISPTMG Skew) on CRTCs 0/3/4, or by setting R6=0 on CRTC 1.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>It is not possible to force DISPTMG on CRTC 2.
                                            </p>
                                            <p>
                                                <br/>
                                            </p>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                    <section id="citizen-section-14" class="citizen-section">
                                        <h3 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                            <span class="mw-headline" id="Border_bytes">Border bytes</span>
                                        </h3>
                                        <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                            <p>Despite their 1MHz clock speed, CRTCs 0/2 have been observed to change state at a rate equivalent to 2MHz chips by responding to both the rising and falling edges of each clock cycle.
                                            </p>
                                            <section id="citizen-section-15" class="citizen-section">
                                                <h4 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="Interline_border">Interline border</span>
                                                </h4>
                                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                                    <p>On CRTCs 0/2, R1>R0 generates one byte (0.5µs) of border at the end of the raster line. On CRTCs 1/3/4, it does not.
                                                    </p>
                                                    <p>To see the border bytes with your own eyes, type this BASIC line after reset:
                                                    </p>
                                                    <pre>BORDER 6:OUT &amp;BC00,6:OUT &amp;BD00,0
                                                    </pre>
                                                </div>
                                            </section>
                                        </div>
                                    </section>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-16" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="HSYNC_and_VSYNC">HSYNC and VSYNC</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>On CPC, HSYNC and VSYNC from the CRTC are passed into the Gate-Array.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>When HSYNC is active Gate-Array outputs the palette colour black. If the HSYNC is set to 14 characters then black will be output for 14us.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The HSYNC is modified before being sent to the monitor. It  happens 2us after the HSYNC from the CRTC and lasts 4us when HSYNC length is greater or equal to 6. 
                                    </p>
                                    <p>If R2=46, and HSYNC width is 14 then monitor hsync starts at 48 and lasts until 51.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>On a CPC monitor, the HSYNC is rendered in "absolute black". It is darker than the black output by the Gate-Array.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>The VSYNC is also modified before being sent to the monitor. It happens two lines* after the VSYNC from the CRTC and stay two lines (same cut rule if VSYNC is lower than 4). PAL (50Hz) does need two lines VSYNC_width, and 4us HSYNC_width.
                                    </p>
                                    <p>Using CRTC1, VSYNC width value 0 means a value of 16.
                                    </p>
                                </div>
                            </section>
                            <section id="citizen-section-17" class="citizen-section">
                                <h2 class="citizen-section-heading">
                                    <span class="mw-headline" id="The_6845_Registers">The 6845 Registers</span>
                                </h2>
                                <div class="citizen-section-body">
                                    <p>The Internal registers of the 6845 are:
                                    </p>
                                    <table border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="margin: 1em 1em 1em 0; background: #f9f9f9; border: 1px #aaa solid; border-collapse: collapse;">
                                        <tbody>
                                            <tr>
                                                <td>
